question: Inhibin: a new circulating marker of hydatidiform mole?
answer: Serum inhibin is elevated in hydatidiform mole: before evacuation, median serum inhibin was 8.3 U/ml versus 2.8 U/ml in normal pregnancy at the same stage, and it fell significantly to follicular-phase levels 7-10 days after evacuation. Molar tissue contains inhibin in high concentrations (median cytosol 578 U/ml), consistent with the tissue being a source of the circulating inhibin. In a study of molar and other placental tumours, inhibin A was raised in 10/17 patients and inhibin B in 4/17, and during chemotherapy inhibin A tracked hCG and free hCG-beta, normalizing faster than hCG-beta in some patients. None of four patients whose post-evacuation inhibin was 0.4 U/ml or lower developed persistent trophoblastic disease, suggesting possible prognostic value.

question: Discharging patients earlier from Winnipeg hospitals: does it adversely affect quality of care?
answer: In Winnipeg's seven large acute care hospitals, length of stay fell significantly (11.1% to 22.0%) across four diagnostic categories over 1989-93 without a consistent rise in 30-day readmission rates, so earlier discharge did not appear to adversely affect quality of care. Physician visits within 30 days after discharge did not rise meaningfully: they increased slightly for AMI in the first year and then stayed flat, and decreased slightly for bronchitis or asthma. Across individual Winnipeg hospitals in 1992-93, length of stay was not significantly correlated with readmission rates in any category, or with physician visits for AMI and bronchitis or asthma. The one exception was uterine or adnexal procedures, where readmission rose significantly between the first and second year but then stayed constant over the next three years.

question: Transesophageal echocardiographic assessment of left ventricular function in brain-dead patients: are marginally acceptable hearts suitable for transplantation?
answer: In a prospective TEE study of 55 potential brain-dead heart donors, hearts with marginal left ventricular function (fractional area change below 50%) were transplanted successfully in most cases: 36 of 40 harvested hearts were successfully transplanted, including 9 from donors with FAC <50%. Survival did not differ significantly between recipients of hearts from donors with FAC >50% and FAC <50% (86.2% vs 64.6% at 1 and 2 years, p = NS), and FAC rose from 51% to 57% in hearts re-examined after transplantation, suggesting donor dysfunction can recover.

question: Vertical lines in distal esophageal mucosa (VLEM): a true endoscopic manifestation of esophagitis in children?
answer: In a retrospective review of pediatric esophageal biopsies, VLEM as the only endoscopic abnormality was associated with histologic esophagitis: only 1 of 41 biopsies (2.4%) was normal, versus 57.5% normal in children with a normal-appearing mucosa. question: Are head and neck specific quality of life measures necessary?
answer: Head and neck-specific health status domains appear to be distinct from general QOL measures: in 55 head and neck cancer patients, the Head&Neck Survey correlated more strongly with other head and neck-specific measures than with a general health measure. Eating/swallowing and speech/communication domains were not well correlated with general health domains, and appearance was not fully reflected by any other domain, so general measures may miss these aspects. Not all domains were distinct: head and neck pain was highly correlated with general bodily pain (r=0.88), suggesting a general measure may capture pain adequately.

question: Does the SCL 90-R obsessive-compulsive dimension identify cognitive impairments?
answer: In 19 adults with malignant brain tumors, the SCL 90-R Obsessive-Compulsive subscale was not related to objective measures of attention, verbal memory, or age, so it did not identify objective cognitive impairment. question: Hypotension in patients with coronary disease: can profound hypotensive events cause myocardial ischaemic events?
answer: In patients with ischaemic heart disease on hypotensive drugs, ST-segment ischaemic events were significantly associated with preceding hypotensive events (chi2 = 40.2, p<0.0001), and 14 hypotension-induced ischaemic events occurred in 8 of 25 patients. Most hypotension-induced ischaemic events (13 of 14) were preceded by a fall in diastolic pressure, and six by a fall in systolic pressure. question: Fatigue in primary Sjögren's syndrome: is there a link with the fibromyalgia syndrome?
answer: Fatigue was common in primary Sjögren's syndrome (68%, 50/74), significantly more than in lupus patients (50%), and fibromyalgia was present in 12% (9/74) of pSS patients versus 5% of lupus patients, suggesting a link between fatigue, pSS and FM. FM was absent in the small subset of lupus patients with secondary Sjögren's syndrome (0/13), although fatigue was present in 54% (7/13) of them, so fatigue was not always accompanied by FM.

question: Is alexithymia a risk factor for unexplained physical symptoms in general medical outpatients?
answer: In a cross-sectional study of general medical outpatients, those with medically unexplained physical symptoms (169 of 321) were overall not more alexithymic than those with explained symptoms, so alexithymia was not supported as a risk factor. question: Is semi-closed endarterectomy of the superficial femoral artery combined with a short venous bypass in case of insufficient venous material an acceptable alternative for limb-threatening ischemia?
answer: In 30 patients with critical leg ischemia and insufficient vein, SFA semiclosed endarterectomy plus short venous bypass gave cumulative primary patency of 60.3% at 1 year and 48.4% at 3 years, with limb salvage of 68.6% at 1 and 3 years. question: Antral follicle assessment as a tool for predicting outcome in IVF--is it a better predictor than age and FSH?
answer: In a prospective study of 224 IVF patients, baseline antral follicle count >6 was associated with a much higher clinical pregnancy rate than count ≤6 (51% vs 19%), and this difference remained significant after controlling for patient age and basal FSH. Cancellation rate was far higher with baseline antral follicles ≤6 than >6 (33% vs 1%); cancellation was also increased with advancing age and elevated basal FSH, but antral follicle count retained an independent association. In a separate cohort of IVF/ICSI pregnancies, AFC was the only ovarian reserve marker (compared with FSH, basal oestradiol and oestradiol response) that differed between miscarriage and ongoing pregnancy groups, though its discriminative ability was low (AUC 0.588).

question: Acute respiratory distress syndrome in children with malignancy--can we predict outcome?
answer: In a retrospective review of 17 children with malignancy and ARDS on mechanical ventilation, outcome could be distinguished early: peak inspiratory pressure, PEEP and ventilation index separated survivors from non-survivors by day 3. Oxygenation efficiency measures (PaO2/FIO2 and P(A-a)O2) were significantly related to outcome only from day 8 after the start of mechanical ventilation, so they were later predictors. Overall mortality in this cohort was high, with only 6 of 17 children (35.3%) surviving, and sepsis syndrome was present in 70.6%.

question: Does tranexamic acid reduce desmopressin-induced hyperfibrinolysis?
answer: In a randomized trial of 100 CABG patients, adding tranexamic acid to desmopressin reduced fibrinolysis markers and bleeding compared with desmopressin alone: fibrin split products were lower (13.5 vs 21.2 ng/mL) and fibrinogen higher (167 vs 113 mg/dL). question: Is specialty care associated with improved survival of patients with congestive heart failure?
answer: In a large VHA retrospective cohort of CHF patients, those with combined general medicine and cardiology (MIXED) follow-up had the best 1-year survival: adjusted risk of death was 1.26 (1.15-1.38) for general-medicine-only care and 1.48 (1.28-1.72) for no GM/cardiology care versus MIXED. question: Can progression of valvar aortic stenosis be predicted accurately?
answer: In a cohort of 169 men and 88 women with aortic stenosis, progression was found to be sufficiently predictable for clinical purposes, depending on the degree of valvar calcification and on the initial hemodynamic severity (transaortic gradient). Progression rate was exponentially correlated with initial aortic valve opening area and depended on calcification grade; specific thresholds (e.g., AVA below 0.75 cm2 with calcification 0, up to 1.0 cm2 with calcification III) indicated that surgery would probably be needed in following years. Age, sex and etiology of the valve obstruction did not significantly influence progression, so prediction can rely mainly on calcification and hemodynamic measures.

question: Sub-classification of low-grade cerebellar astrocytoma: is it clinically meaningful?
answer: In a Danish cohort of children with cerebellar astrocytoma followed 15-40 years, no survival difference was found between pilocytic and fibrillary astrocytoma, so histological sub-classification did not appear prognostically meaningful. question: Juvenile ankylosing spondylitis--is it the same disease as adult ankylosing spondylitis?
answer: In a retrospective review of 210 Indian patients with ankylosing spondylitis, juvenile-onset disease (onset before age 17) differed from adult-onset disease in presentation, suggesting they are not identical in clinical expression. question: Is eligibility for a chemotherapy protocol a good prognostic factor for invasive bladder cancer after radical cystectomy?
answer: In a study of patients undergoing radical cystectomy for invasive bladder cancer, those eligible for and entered into an adjuvant chemotherapy protocol (SAKK 09/84) had better outcomes than age- and stage-matched non-protocol patients and the remaining patients, with median overall survival of 76.3 vs 52.1 vs 20.3 months. question: Is gastric electrical stimulation superior to standard pharmacologic therapy in improving GI symptoms, healthcare resources, and long-term health care benefits?
answer: In a 3-year comparison of gastroparesis patients, gastric electrical stimulation (GES) showed more sustained GI symptom improvement over 36 months than intensive medical therapy. question: Chemotherapy and survival in advanced non-small cell lung carcinoma: is pneumologists' skepticism justified?
answer: In a study of 190 patients with advanced NSCLC (stage IV or IIIB), cytostatic treatment was an independent predictor of survival (HR 1.85, 95% CI 1.25-2.76, P=.002), suggesting skepticism about chemotherapy's real-world benefit is not justified. answer: In a Swedish population-based cohort, daughters and sisters of a proband with poor breast cancer prognosis had a 60% higher 5-year breast cancer mortality than those of a proband with good prognosis (HR 1.6, 95% CI 1.2-2.2), suggesting prognosis aggregates in families. question: Is laparoscopic adrenalectomy safe and effective for adrenal masses larger than 7 cm?

question: Are adult body circumferences associated with height?
answer: In NHANES III adults, waist and hip circumferences were significantly associated with height after adjustment for age and race, scaling with powers of 0.76 and 0.45 in men and 0.80 and 0.53 in women, which corresponds to about 0.2 to 0.5 cm more circumference per cm of height. question: Does minimal access major surgery in the newborn hurt less?
answer: In a retrospective matched cohort of neonates undergoing thoracoscopic repair of esophageal atresia or congenital diaphragmatic hernia, cumulative postoperative opioid doses did not differ significantly from conventional surgery at 12 h, 24 h, 48 h or 7 days. question: Can dobutamine stress echocardiography induce cardiac troponin elevation?

question: Are patients with serious mental illness more likely to be admitted to nursing homes with more deficiencies in care?

question: Is endometrial polyp formation associated with increased expression of vascular endothelial growth factor and transforming growth factor-beta1?
answer: In a prospective study of 70 premenopausal women, endometrial polyps showed higher VEGF and TGF-β1 expression than adjacent endometrium, so polyp formation is associated with increased expression of both. question: Does a colonoscopy after acute diverticulitis affect its management?
answer: In a retrospective review of 100 patients who had early (4-6 week) colonoscopy after acute diverticulitis, no colonic malignancy was found and no new or different diagnosis resulted, suggesting colonoscopy did not change management. question: Globulomaxillary cysts--do they really exist?

question: Does the sex of acute stroke patients influence the effectiveness of rt-PA?
answer: In 369 rt-PA-treated stroke patients with TCD monitoring, men and women did not differ in complete, partial, or no recanalization (p=0.6), nor in time to recanalization or 3-month clinical outcome after adjustment. question: Is there any relation between cervical cord plaques and discopathy in patients with multiple sclerosis?
answer: In a retrospective study of 536 MS patients, cervical cord plaques were located at the same site as cervical discopathy significantly more often than at different sites. question: Do emergency ultrasound fellowship programs impact emergency medicine residents' ultrasound education?
answer: In a cross-sectional study of 244 EM residents at 9 academic centers, residents in programs with EUS fellowships reported performing more ultrasound scans than those in programs without fellowships (P = .04). question: Is scintigraphy a guideline method in determining amputation levels in diabetic foot?
answer: The only study directly addressing scintigraphy for amputation level in diabetic foot (30 patients) used 3-phase bone scintigraphy, marking the most distal perfused site as the amputation level, alongside Doppler ultrasound and intraoperative inspection; it reported varied amputation levels, reamputation in 7 patients, and no mortality.

question: HIF1A as a major vascular endothelial growth factor regulator: do its polymorphisms have an association with age-related macular degeneration?
answer: In a study of 87 AMD patients and 80 controls, no statistically significant difference emerged in the distribution of the HIF1A polymorphisms rs11549465 and rs11549467 between patients and healthy subjects. question: May student examiners be reasonable substitute examiners for faculty in an undergraduate OSCE on medical emergencies?
answer: In a randomized comparison of 207 third-year students in an emergency medicine OSCE, student examiners and faculty examiners produced broadly comparable results: students scored higher with student examiners on 3 of 7 stations (TM, AM, OE) and on overall score, and lower on 1 station (PE), mostly with small effect sizes. question: Is vitamin D insufficiency or deficiency related to the development of osteochondritis dissecans?
answer: In a prospective pilot study of 23 patients with stage III/IV osteochondritis dissecans (OCD) lesions, 18 had a distinct vitamin D3 deficiency, 2 were insufficient, and 3 were at the lowest normal level, so nearly all had low or borderline vitamin D. question: Does radiotherapy of the primary rectal cancer affect prognosis after pelvic exenteration for recurrent rectal cancer?
answer: In a retrospective review of 87 patients undergoing pelvic exenteration for locally recurrent rectal cancer, prior radiotherapy for the primary tumour was associated with worse prognosis, including lower disease-free survival (p = 0.022). question: Rectal cancer threatening or affecting the prostatic plane: is partial prostatectomy oncologically adequate?
answer: In a multicentre retrospective series of 126 men with rectal cancer threatening or affecting the prostatic plane, partial prostatectomy after preoperative chemoradiotherapy gave a free anterior circumferential resection margin in all cases, and overall CRM positivity after chemoradiotherapy plus prostatic resection was 2.4%. question: Living in an urban environment and non-communicable disease risk in Thailand: Does timing matter?

question: Literacy after cerebral hemispherectomy: Can the isolated right hemisphere read?
answer: In seven people who had left hemispherectomy for seizures tied to perinatal infarct, about 60% developed average-range word reading and paragraph reading, so the isolated right hemisphere can support reading in many cases. question: Preparing patients at high risk of falls for discharge home after rehabilitation: Do we meet the guidelines?
answer: Guidelines were not fully met: in a retrospective audit of 50 high-falls-risk rehabilitation patients discharged home, discharge documentation correctly identified falls risk for only nine of them. question: MR Diagnosis of Bone Metastases at 1.5 T and 3 T: Can STIR Imaging Be Omitted?

question: Does cup-cage reconstruction with oversized cups provide initial stability in THA for osteoporotic acetabular fractures?

question: Utility of unenhanced fat-suppressed T1-weighted MRI in children with sickle cell disease -- can it differentiate bone infarcts from acute osteomyelitis?

question: Are financial incentives cost-effective to support smoking cessation during pregnancy?

question: Do Wound Cultures Give Information About the Microbiology of Blood Cultures in Severe Burn Patients?

question: Treatment of contralateral hydrocele in neonatal testicular torsion: Is less more?

question: Could chest wall rigidity be a factor in rapid death from illicit fentanyl abuse?

question: Do risk calculators accurately predict surgical site occurrences?
answer: Existing risk calculators did not accurately predict surgical site occurrences after open ventral hernia repair: in a multicenter retrospective database (n=795), AUCs for SSO were low (0.52-0.60) across the VHRS, VHWG, CDC Wound Class and HW-RAT. question: Does the familial transmission of drinking patterns persist into young adulthood?

question: Does the treatment of amblyopia normalise subfoveal choroidal thickness in amblyopic children?
answer: Six months of amblyopia treatment did not normalise subfoveal choroidal thickness in anisometropic hyperopic amblyopic children: pre- vs post-treatment thickness did not differ significantly in amblyopic eyes (p = 0.428), and thickness remained higher than in fellow eyes after treatment (p = 0.006). Visual acuity improved significantly with treatment (mean 0.35 to 0.16 logMAR, p < 0.001), so the choroidal thickness did not change despite visual improvement. Before treatment, choroidal thickness was significantly greater in amblyopic eyes than in fellow eyes (p = 0.019), and fellow eyes also showed no significant change after treatment (p = 0.343).

question: Prostate bed target interfractional motion using RTOG consensus definitions and daily CT on rails : Does target motion differ between superior and inferior portions of the clinical target volume?
answer: Target motion did not differ significantly between the superior and inferior prostate bed CTV in any direction (LR, SI, AP) using daily CT-on-rails and RTOG-defined volumes. Mean INF-CTV target motion was 0.1, 0.5 and 0.2 mm in LR, SI and AP directions, while SUP-CTV motion was 0.3, 0.5 and 0 mm; the SUP-CTV AP variability (SD 5.0 mm) was larger than that of INF-CTV (SD 2.5 mm), though not significantly different.

question: Do prerecorded lecture VODcasts affect lecture attendance of first-yearpre-clinical Graduate Entry to Medicine students?
answer: Providing prerecorded VODcasts did not appear to reduce live lecture attendance among first-year GEM students: 84.3% attended all 21 Physiology lectures and only 4% missed more than one lecture in each lecture series. Most students (79%) indicated that VODcasts should not replace live lectures.

question: Are serum leptin levels a prognostic factor in advanced lung cancer?
answer: In 71 previously untreated lung cancer patients, serum leptin levels showed no association with overall survival, so leptin was not found to be a prognostic factor. Serum leptin did not differ significantly by ECOG performance status, weight loss, histological type, disease stage or TNM classification, though it correlated with BMI. Leptin levels were lower in lung cancer patients than in matched controls, so leptin differs at diagnosis but without showing prognostic value in this study.
